fixes.explanation: Yes, baker! “As Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). The cloud settles at the door, and then the LORD speaks. Verse 7 says anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to this tent outside the camp. Moses walks in, and he isn't left standing there wondering.

Nice try, friend, but nobody's grabbing a pen in this scene. The verse says, “…the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). Moses walks in, the cloud comes down, and the LORD does the talking. I'd have been standing there with my mustache hanging open, no notes taken.

Yes, friend. “When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.” (Exodus 33:10). They didn't have to walk to the tent. Verse 8 says they would stand at their own tent entrances and watch Moses until he went in, so they were already right there. Front row seats, and nobody had to fight for parking.

Yes, baker! “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). That line is the heart of the scene. It's like two friends talking across the counter, with nobody in between. Right after it, Moses speaks to the LORD and the LORD answers him (Exodus 33:12).

That's him! “…his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.” (Exodus 33:11). Moses heads back to camp, but Joshua stays put in the tent. The text doesn't say why he stayed, and I'd love to know. I bet I would have stayed too, wouldn't you?

Careful, baker, Moses isn't being sent off solo. The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). Notice who's doing the going: it's His own Presence. Moses was worried about who would go with him, and that's the very thing this answer settles. Walking a long road alone is rough, and I've spent years alone in a drawer, so trust me on that.

That's right, baker. Moses asks, “For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us?” (Exodus 33:16). Moses isn't asking for a trophy or a parade. He wants the proof of God's favor to be God Himself walking with them. If you've ever wanted the real thing and not just a nice sticker on the box, you get Moses here.

Yes, friend. Moses asks, “How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?” (Exodus 33:16). In his words, God going with them is what sets them apart from every other people. Think of a batch where one cookie is the only one stamped by the master. Everybody can tell which one it is.

That's it, friend. Moses asked to see His glory, and the LORD answers with what He will do. He says, “…I will proclaim My name” (Exodus 33:19). He also says He will cause all His goodness to pass before Moses. So Moses gets to hear the name spoken, right there in his presence.

That's right. The LORD says, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). That's the reason He gives, and it's a serious one. He doesn't say no and leave it there, though. In the next verses He tells Moses where to stand on a rock and what He will do (Exodus 33:21, 22, 23).

Yes, baker! The LORD says, “Then I will take My hand away, and you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). Before that, He says He will put Moses in a cleft of the rock and cover him with His hand until He has passed by (Exodus 33:22). So Moses gets covered first, then he sees. I think if I were standing in that rock, I'd be holding very, very still.
